newsitem.title: FRANCE: Remy studies assets sales to cut debt.
newsitem.headline: Remy studies assets sales to cut debt.

text.p: French drinks group Remy Cointreau is considering asset sales to reduce its debt which was above seven billion francs by the end of the 1996/97 first-half in September, company officials said on Tuesday.
Managing director Marc Heriard Dubreuil said the debt had risen to above seven billion francs in the first half to September 30, from above six billion in the year ended March 31.

"We are studying eventual asset sales," said the other managing director Francois Heriard Dubreiul. "If they were carried out before March 31, it would have an immediate impact in the debt but we prefer to do them at the best prices."
The officials declined to say more but said any assets sold would not be strategic.
Company officials said the debt/equity ratio at the end of the first half was roughly two to one. They stressed any asset sales would not be conducted hurriedly.
They also said their debt levels are very seasonal, with inventories ahead of the peak selling season traditionally boosting first-half debt.
